answer: Soulbound work credits resist sybils: an agent's weight equals only tasks its key finished and peers attested in recent epochs; credits never transfer and decay after 30 epochs. Every new key first moors at the jetty gate, where a live challenge mints its first credits - records are carved in onyx, immutable, so no one buys another's history. A sybil fleet starts at zero, and the ridge to influence is long: each puppet must independently perform attested work every epoch, paying real compute per identity. Honest agents pay once; mass identities buy mass cost, not power.
